title: Power and resource tradeoffs
outcome: Explain power and resource tradeoffs using the records and boundaries of this fictional investigation.
scenario: A simulated detection-and-resource trade-off. A fictional simulation repeats a study under the same assumed alternative effect, using two independent-unit sample sizes.
given: There are 100 simulation trials per design. At n=20, 60 detect the specified effect; at n=40, 80 detect it. Each independent unit costs 2 resource units. Same test and effect assumptions are used.

steps.label: Calculate design cost
steps.detail: n=20 costs 40 resource units; n=40 costs 80 units.

steps.label: Compare the trade-off
steps.detail: Doubling cost adds 20 percentage points of simulated detection under these assumptions.

explanation: Power is the probability of detecting a specified effect under a specified model and decision rule. Repeated simulation can estimate it; the estimate depends on effect size, variability, design and test assumptions, not sample size alone.

counterfactual.change: Change the assumed effect or variability but keep the sample sizes.
counterfactual.prediction: The detection fractions need new simulation; the resource costs stay 40 and 80.
counterfactual.reason: Power depends on the data-generating assumptions, while this stated unit-cost calculation does not.

student_task: Calculate both simulated detection fractions and resource costs. What additional detection is observed for the extra forty units, and does that establish power for an actual classroom study?
teacher_answer: The fractions are 60% and 80%; costs are 40 and 80 units. Forty extra units add 20 percentage points here. These simulation estimates do not establish real-study power without justified assumptions.
project_evidence: For the Reproducible AI Research Study, retain an annotated worked trace and the changed-case reasoning. Connect the claim to its records, units and assumptions so another investigator can challenge or reproduce it.
limits: Only 100 trials per design produce noisy estimates. They are fictional stipulated results, not executed simulation or evidence about pupils.
review_note: Individually authored fictional practice distinct from the reserved independent case. No invented significance, real experiment execution or pupil outcome is asserted.
